> In my research, I am using the attached model. Treating the model
> exactly as displayed returns the covariance matrix between y1 and y2 as
> 0.000. However, in previous iterations where I used y1 and y2 as

> 'polycor' package on R, I checked the polychoric correlation of y1 and
> y2 and it is equal to 0.44.
>
> Why could the correlation be estimated to 0.000 instead of its true value?

Not sure. Can you provide a reproducible example?

> Also, whether in the attached case or - let's say - in an "all variable
> are continuous case", how do the correlation between the two enter the
> estimation process? Is it through the variance-covariance matrix of the
> error measurements which is a part of the implied covariance matrix?

I did not understand your question. Can you rephrase, perhaps using an
example?

Yves.
